target_customer: Auto lenders such as banks, credit unions and finance companies that must file and release liens with state DMVs
problem: Filing a lien with a DMV varies by state and county and is manual, slow and error prone for auto lenders.
business_model: B2B SaaS and API priced per filing or contract

founders.name: Jack Chapman
founders.background_notes: The YC page lists no background.

founders.name: Muhammad Khattak
founders.background_notes: R&D engineer at Veridise per the YC page.

founders.name: Grant Pease
founders.background_notes: Also listed under former founders on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Mapping state and county specific forms and DMV or electronic lien and title interfaces is laborious integration work, with document extraction using language models.

defensibility.rationale: Coverage of all 50 states, integrations into lender loan systems and a MeridianLink partnership create switching costs, though the content could be rebuilt by a funded competitor.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquisition or copying by incumbents was found.

market_need_then: Lenders must file liens on every secured auto loan across inconsistent state processes. The company later claimed over 10 billion dollars in filings and customers such as Capital One and OneMain, as stated on the YC page.

identity.logo: Not described by any source opened

brand_strength.rationale: No press on the brand was found. Search for the name returns unrelated companies named Cardinal.

outcome_analysis: Cardinal Gray is an active four person YC S23 company serving large auto lenders with lien filing automation and a MeridianLink partnership. Funding is not publicly verified, so the scale of its progress is unclear, but the customer list claimed by the company suggests real traction.
notes: Aggregators (VCBacked, CB Insights) report 500K total, pre-seed or convertible note, from Y Combinator, Eight Capital and Unpopular Ventures around 2023, both aggregators and unverified, so no round is recorded. The YC launch post says the original application was rejected in an earlier batch. No competitor sources dated near 2023 were found. CB Insights lists CHAMP, SafeWire and AbstractOps as later competitors, undated. YC pages disagree on team size and location.
